LESSON: FAMILIES IN OUR NEIGHBOURHOOD

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Neighbourhood
Topic 4.1: Families in Our Neighbourhood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Families in Our Neighbourhood, part of Our Neighbourhood in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we identify our neighbour?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Families in Our Neighbourhood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: learner develops speaking skills when talking about families in the neighbourhood.

Values:
Respect: learner respects others when dramatising families in the neighbourhood.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion: learner enhances cohesion when reciting poems on families in the neighbourhood.

Link to other learning areas:

Families in the neighbourhood relates to the concepts of loving your neighbourhood in Religious Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures and picture cut outs about families in the neighbourhood, theme-based multi- purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices, songs and poems about families in the neighbourhood, universal cuffs

with padded pencils, crayons with grips, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using lower extremities, book holders and page

turners, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/

crutches, head/ mouth pointers, splints for hands/ hand stabilizers,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe
